Dear Arthur,

First of all let me wish you and everyone a happy new year!
I still haven't figured out why it's NULL.
I found this contradiction.

> aa.genlight@ploidy
NULL
BUT if I try
> ploidy(aa.genlight)
ever23974 ever26575 ever26837 ever34843 ever35050 everLaE01 everMev01 everZH030 everZH104 hybr26626

        2         2         2         2         2         2         2         2         2         2

hybr26714 hybrCs010 puto26835  puto3szR putoDMP23 putoDMP24  putoP01R putoSMP14 putoSMP15 putoZH106

        2         2         2         2         2         2         2         2         2         2

putoZH136 putoZH138
        2         2

I know it is not a DartR issue, but would you be so kind to helpme with that, because i run out of ideas?

Many thanks
Lajos

messages.subject: gl.recode.pop bug
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I’m having trouble renaming my sites in my genlight file with the gl.recode.pop function, and wonder if there is a bug? I get the same error for both my data and also bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl> or testset.gl <http://testset.gl>.

I can create a draft recode table via the gl.make.recode.pop function and edit it in excel, or even RStudio. However, when I use it to run gl.recode.pop my pops are labelled as numbers. The function seems to be treating them as factors. I even get the error if I don’t edit the recode table.

I can repeat the whole process, but recoding individuals with the very similar gl.recode.ind function and have no problem.

Delving inexpertly into some of the code for these two functions, one difference I see is that @ line 83 gl.recode.ind sets stringsAsFactors=FALSE, whereas gl.recode.pop has stringsAsFactors = TRUE @ line 87. If I edit that code to be stringsAsFactors = TRUE and rerun using my edited version of the function, I seem to be able to get it to work properly.

What do you think Arthur/Bernd?

Cheers,

Olly

My code is as follows:

gl.make.recode.pop(working.gl <http://working.gl>, out.recode.file = "testpop.csv", outpath = getwd())

working.gl <http://working.gl> <- gl.recode.pop(working.gl <http://working.gl>, pop.recode = "testpop.csv", recalc = FALSE, mono.rm = FALSE, verbose = 5)

levels(working.gl <http://working.gl>$pop)

messages.subject: RE: gl.recode.pop bug
messages.body_plain:
Hi Olly,

This seems to be an error that came in with R 4. Because here the default is stringsAsFactors = FALSE when using read.csv, which is not what you want in most cases from our point of view. Here I think we made a mistake and it needs be set to FALSE as you suggested.

Will be in the next update (Luis is starting the coming week 😊)

Cheers, Bernd

Subject: [dartR] gl.recode.pop bug

Hi,

I’m having trouble renaming my sites in my genlight file with the gl.recode.pop function, and wonder if there is a bug? I get the same error for both my data and also bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl> or testset.gl <http://testset.gl>.

I can create a draft recode table via the gl.make.recode.pop function and edit it in excel, or even RStudio. However, when I use it to run gl.recode.pop my pops are labelled as numbers. The function seems to be treating them as factors. I even get the error if I don’t edit the recode table.

I can repeat the whole process, but recoding individuals with the very similar gl.recode.ind function and have no problem.

Delving inexpertly into some of the code for these two functions, one difference I see is that @ line 83 gl.recode.ind sets stringsAsFactors=FALSE, whereas gl.recode.pop has stringsAsFactors = TRUE @ line 87. If I edit that code to be stringsAsFactors = TRUE and rerun using my edited version of the function, I seem to be able to get it to work properly.

What do you think Arthur/Bernd?

Cheers,

Olly

My code is as follows:

gl.make.recode.pop(working.gl <http://working.gl>, out.recode.file = "testpop.csv", outpath = getwd())

working.gl <http://working.gl> <- gl.recode.pop(working.gl <http://working.gl>, pop.recode = "testpop.csv", recalc = FALSE, mono.rm = FALSE, verbose = 5)

levels(working.gl <http://working.gl>$pop)

Hi Olly,

This seems to be an error that came in with R 4. Because here the default is stringsAsFactors = FALSE when using read.csv, which is not what you want in most cases from our point of view. He

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] RE: gl.recode.pop bug
messages.body_plain:
Yes, R changed the default, and we had to go through all scripts to resolve. Seems like we made a mistake with this one. Will fix for the next version.

messages.subject: New dartR member
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

first a happy new year from us to all of you. We have good news as we have a new staff member starting this week who is meant to work on dartR and support its development. His name is Luis and feel free to contact us/him either via the google groups here or via github (if you have a issue please try to log it there). Contrary to previous responses these will be quicker I hope.

There will be more from us in the coming days where we outline how we think we want to develop the package and how we aim to get you involved.

All the best and cheers,

Bernd & Luis & Arthur
